speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The original motto of the Olympics was adopted in 1894 and coined by the Founder of the modern Olympic Games, Pierre de Coubertin.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is "citius", "altius" and "fortius" in Latin – and I hope I have not butchered it.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Or as we know it better in English: "faster", "higher", "stronger".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: What is less known is that after 127 years, in 2021, the motto was slightly modified to "citius, altius, fortius, communiter". "Communiter" is Latin for "together".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, the current motto of the Olympics is really "faster, higher, stronger, together". "Together" is also why we are here today in this House to pass this Motion to celebrate our Olympians and Paralympians.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They are with us in this House observing the proceedings.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We thank them and their loved ones for their presence.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But more importantly, we thank them for bringing us together as a community, as a nation, in a way that only they can, through sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They have engendered a sense of "togetherness" that is so important for a young nation like Singapore to experience as part of our nation-building.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The adjectives "faster", "higher" and "stronger" are known as comparative adjectives in English grammar.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They are commonly used to compare one person or a team against another person or another team.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But there is another deeper dimension to this, especially with the addition of the word "together" in the motto.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Forty years ago, in the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, American sprint legend, Carl Lewis, won the men's 100-metre sprint with a time of 9.99 seconds.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2024, the same event was won by American sprinter, Noah Lyles, at 9.79 seconds.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In fact, he won it by 5000th of a second.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I am not sure the human eye or brain could process it.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But more importantly, the slowest qualifying time for the men's 100-metre final at Paris 2024 was 9.91 seconds, which means if legend Carl Lewis had run the same race in 2024 as he did in 1984 to win the gold, he would not have even qualified for the Finals in Paris.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This, Sir, is progress for athletics and it is also progress for the human race.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: When we compete in a friendly and fair manner repeatedly over time, everyone in the field improves.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Fair and friendly competition is good for everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They competed against the world's best, carrying the weight of our nation's hopes and dreams.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They stood out, not just as individuals, but also represented Singapore's collective aspirations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I had the privilege of attending the 2024 Paris Olympics and Paralympics, where I witnessed firsthand our athletes' determination and resolve, even as they stood up against formidable opponents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Not all our Olympians and Paralympians present today won a medal in Paris.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They have all fought hard in the toughest of arenas and pushed themselves above and beyond their limits.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As Jesse Owens, another Olympic legend, once said, "The only victory that counts is the one over yourself." And our athletes have achieved this victory.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They have not just represented our nation with distinction, but they have conquered themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And we thank, and we honour, Team Singapore athletes for being our source of inspiration and for being our role models.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: What resonates with us, though, goes well beyond tangible medal achievements.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: More important is the resilience we saw in their attitudes and the grace with which they have conducted themselves and flown our flag so proudly.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, we have Jeralyn Tan, our first Paralympic silver medallist for boccia.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Her story is about conviction and perseverance, sticking through the tough times.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In her early years of competing, she faced multiple setbacks and losses.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: After several years of hard work and winning three editions of the World Boccia Cup in 2023 and 2024, she is now the world's top-ranked boccia player in her class.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: She qualified for the Paralympics this year, and as you would know, she came back with the historic first medal in boccia, winning the silver.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I would add that she was a whisker away from the gold – it went down to the very last ball.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But I am sure this will only inspire and motivate Jeralyn even more in future editions of the Paralympics.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, our Olympic bronze medallist, kitefoiler, Max Maeder.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Max's story is about courage and sportsmanship and being an inspirational role model for our youths in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I am sure all of you will remember that Max gave Singapore a wonderful birthday present on National Day this year, winning the bronze medal.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We saw his determination and sportsmanship when he came up against world-class opponents, older and more experienced than him.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But Members, if you get a chance to have a chat with this fine young gentleman, you will be struck by his passion, his maturity, and his humility at his young age.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Max's story shows that we can, and indeed, every Singaporean must dare to dream big and chase the rainbow, no matter the odds, and of course, as he has shown, no matter the age.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, Yip Pin Xiu – our double-gold medallist in swimming.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is one of consistency and longevity at the highest level, but also about selfless service to the community and to our nation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But perhaps what is more remarkable is how she uses her standing and her sporting achievements to champion causes that she believes in.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Pin Xiu has made extensive contributions to our nation, as a passionate advocate on social issues – on youths, on sports, on inclusion for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In fact, just over the weekend, she was out at the Purple Parade!

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Her stint as a former Nominated Member of Parliament, a current National Youth Council member, and a member of the SDSC Board among others – that is a testament of her selfless service to the community in a broad and diverse range of different sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I want to add my congratulations to all our medal winners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But we only saw the tip of the iceberg or the sharp end of the spear as it were.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: An event like athletics or swimming can be over in 10 seconds.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But we saw Team Singapore give their all in every event they competed in, leaving nothing behind in the cauldron of competition in Paris.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But it is not just their efforts alone.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Behind each of them lies an entire support system that has enabled them to be at their very best against the very best in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We all know the saying that it takes a village to raise a child.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But I think it takes more than a village – in this case, maybe a whole town – to raise an athlete to compete and challenge at the highest levels.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This includes their families, the coaches, trainers, physiotherapists, nutritionists, psychologists, sports administrators and even sport associations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: All of them collectively play an important role, creating an environment that enables our athletes to thrive.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I would therefore like to express my deep appreciation to these people who are often unnamed, work quietly behind the scenes in the background, no fuss, to make things happen perfectly for our athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They are a key part of Team Singapore, and an integral part of our success at these Olympics and Paralympics.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And it is indeed a victory founded on the Olympic spirit of "togetherness".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Their collective efforts have enabled our athletes to better themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And I thought it would be useful to give come colour to what I am saying with some examples for Members.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: She is Jeralyn's coach and has has been for many years.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But she is not just a coach, she is also Jeralyn's closest confidant, throughout her long journey.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Their relationship spans many years, and they were involved in countless competitions – locally as well as abroad.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the Paralympics, at the end of her quarter-finals match, Jeralyn was up against the world number one in the quarter finals.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We saw a very astute strategic suggestion that coach gave to Jeralyn which Jeralyn executed to perfection.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: From a defensive position, she pulled off a stunning shot, unerring in accuracy and perfect in weight.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It completely closed off her opponent's angles and frustrated all of her opponent's remaining shots.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This move, which was brilliant, won Jeralyn the match.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Eventually, she made it to the finals where she won the silver.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Coach Yurnita had to judge not just what would work in the context of strategy in the match, but more importantly, whether in that situation, could Jeralyn pull it off.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The coach's deep bond and understanding with Jeralyn allowed her to make the right call at the right time for the athlete.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In the coach's own words, the both of them are "not just like friends; we are like family".

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I saw this myself at the Paralympics – Yurnita celebrated every success and cried every tear, along with Jeralyn.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This deep connection and trust allowed them to navigate both triumphs and challenges successfully together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are fortunate to have coaches like coach Yurnita as part of Team Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Members might not know either that we had a very strong support team for Paris but sitting in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They worked in Singapore, operating from a different time zone.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These included our sport scientists as well as our medical team.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They worked off videos and live data that were sent across, sometimes overnight, from Paris.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They worked round the clock to analyse the data, make suggestions to ensure that our athletes peak, stay at their peak, and were able to compete in a high-pressure and unrelenting environment – everything from sleep to nutrition, physiotherapy to psychology.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They and many more are the invaluable unseen force behind our Team Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Many turned up in full force to celebrate the open-top bus parades a couple of weeks ago.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Some even turned up in Paris, on their own, to lend their support and voices in person.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And we received many more countless messages from Singaporeans, cheering them on in spirit.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I am sure our athletes appreciated every single one of these expressions of support.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also achieved podium success in four out of five editions of the Olympics.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As our Prime Minister said at the National Day Rally, we must find a way to build on these successes and for sport to be a key pathway to success.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, how do we now build on our strong foundations and strive towards our next bound of sporting excellence?

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For starters, we have no time to lose.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Los Angeles 2028 and Brisbane 2032 will be upon us in no time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Renowned American Car Racer Bobby Unser Jr said it well when he said: “Success is where preparation and opportunity meet”.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have to work hard, so that when that opportunity arrives, we will be prepared to make a success of it.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We want today’s athletes to be the giants on whose shoulders our tomorrow's athletes stand.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So that we can also achieve more, with each succeeding generation of Team Singapore athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our first strategy starts at the base, driving keen interest and wide participation in sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: On the whole, Singaporeans have embraced the value of participating in sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are not yet satisfied, we will press on.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Not just to broaden but to deepen participation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our ActiveSG academies and clubs allows youths to take part in a variety of affordable sports programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These programmes are held in our network of Sports Centres right across Singapore, covering 10 different sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Key to increasing sports access to our youths is also our partnership with the Ministry of Education (MOE).

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, MOE and SportSG run the Strategic-Partnership CCA programme, for example in sports like water polo and athletics, to allow students with otherwise no access to these co-curricular activities (CCAs) to be able to take part in and participate in these sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also opened the Sports Hub for more National School Games Finals.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A record number of National School Game events, now take place at the Sports Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We want to allow our children to experience playing in the same venue as the national team.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: An experience that they will not easily forget and will hopefully inspire them for years to come.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) is committed to working with MOE to improving our talent pathways through policies like the Direct School Admission.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This must be complemented by each of our national sports associations' (NSAs’) efforts to broaden the appeal of their sport.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Make it attractive and accessible, build up demand for it so that more schools will offer these sports to start with.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For the community, we have also built up a vibrant community sporting calendar with competitions like the ActiveSG Cup and Pesta Sukan.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I hope some Members here have had the opportunity to take part in those events at the grassroots level.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These events not just allow us to take part in a sport that is healthy, driving participation, but also helps us to bring the community together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have also established, over time, a network of world-class sports facilities that are located closer to all of us, in our neighbourhoods, removing that one last excuse of the centres and facilities being too far away.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For example, our refreshed sports centres at Delta and Choa Chu Kang, our future developments like Toa Payoh and Punggol.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We now cannot complain that the facilities are too far away.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our second strategy is to strengthen our high-performance sport system to be athlete-focused and to give our best athletes the best preparation possible.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our sports institutions like the Singapore Sport Institute (SSI) and National Youth Sports Institute (NYSI) work closely with our NSAs to provide our athletes with the best training environment, every day on a daily basis.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also want to give our athletes access to the best facilities, the top coaches, world-class competitions as well as to benefit from end-to-end sports science support.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Take our top athletes like Swimmer Sophie or Shooter Xiu Hong who are in the Chamber here today.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The spexScholarship that they are on unlocks their potential, gives them a base, providing monthly stipends and dedicated sports science support, allowing them to be fully focused, invested in their sport, training, competing, full-time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also recognise that our top athletes must be constantly challenged.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And so, we send our athletes to train and to compete overseas regularly, allowing our athletes to spar with some of the world's best.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They were able to participate in a range of camps and competitions, in the lead-up to the Olympics.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In fact, prior to being in Paris, they spent an extensive period in Shimada City, Japan, before the 2024 World Table Tennis Team Championships.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This has been one of our most successful high-performance pillars.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, we extended the spex support for our athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, more athletes on the programme covering a bigger range, a wider range, of different sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Collectively, the spexScholars form the core of our Paris Olympics and Paralympics contingent.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Overall, Sir, an enhanced spex support, twinned with the programme at Singapore Sports School provides a comprehensive pathway for our youths to achieve their sporting programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Established 20 years ago now, the Singapore Sports School provides a unique educational offering, wrapping academics around sports, optimising student-athletes’ development in sports whilst at the same time ensuring that they have the best opportunity to maintain their academic pursuits.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Indeed, the Sports School’s results speak for themselves on the sporting stage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This helps take care of a very important aspect of our athlete's needs – academic qualifications and financial stability.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We did so because we know how much our athletes sacrifice when they pursue their sporting ambition.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These initiatives therefore provide our athletes the assurance that their education and financial needs can be supported as they journey on their sporting ambition.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This helps them maintain and remain committed to sports in the long term.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our third strategy is to enhance our institutional capabilities in every aspect of sporting support.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: From cutting-edge sports scientists, to world-class coaches, to technical officials, as examples.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, our sport scientists are playing an increasingly crucial role in preparing our athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I gave some examples earlier of how we operated out of Singapore, supporting our athletes in Paris.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: What they do off the field of play, has a very important and significant bearing on our athletes’ performances.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also know all too well how a good coach makes all the difference.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And so we support the NSA when they identify a good coach they wish to bring in and help us, overall, in our Singapore sporting system, to grow.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, when Fencing Singapore wanted to bring in a world-class coach in Oleg Matshuchiek, we supported them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He was previously with the Japanese national team.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He led them to two Olympic silver medals.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Today, he is part of Team Singapore, focused on training our fencers and turning them into world-class athletes competing with the best on the world's best platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will continue working with our NSAs to develop, identify and bring in the best coaches, to benefit not just our athletes but also develop our own local coaching talent.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We must also build up sporting thought leadership.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We had at least 10 technical officials at the Paris Olympics, representing Singapore in sports such as hockey, gymnastics and diving.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Their expertise and their know-how help us, in turn to lift our sporting standards.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It also profiles Singapore sport on the world stage and positions us to host world-class sporting events in the future.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A number of our former athletes have also become our sports specialists.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We tap into their experience and know-how and the fact that they are very familiar with the circuit.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Former shuttler, Kelvin Ho, is now our singles head coach for our shuttlers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And our former Olympic sailor, Mr Xu Yuan Zhen, was the assistant team manager, for our sailors Ryan and Max.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I watched Yuan Zhen in action – he brought all of his Olympic experience to bear, preparing, mentoring our young sailors, giving them an idea as to what is going to happen, how to take control of the situation, how to deal with the mental aspect of the sport, so that they all gain a competitive advantage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will therefore build up this talent, retain our ex-sportsmen and sportswomen as much as possible, keep them in this space, leverage off the experience that they have and hope to make sports a viable career for each of them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our fourth strategy is to bring in world-class sporting events into Singapore, where we can.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Not just for sporting spectatorship value but also to provide more opportunities for our national athletes to compete and measure themselves against the world’s best, such as for Izaac Quek when he was 16 years old.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He first competed in the 2022 edition of Singapore Smash, one of the more prestigious events in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He lost that match in 2022, but he picked up very important big match experience which would otherwise have been difficult for a young boy about to breakthrough, to master.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He came back stronger a year later, 2023, same competition, Singapore Smash.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He was drawn against the reigning Commonwealth gold medallist.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: He was two sets down, but he came back to win 3-2 and he progressed further in Smash that year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Later that year, he won three SEA Games gold medals and this year, in July, he made his debut at the Olympics.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: You can see the value of having world-class events in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We get wildcards for our athletes, they take part, they compete, they participate, they gain the experience and then, their improvement is exponential.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our fifth strategy is to strengthen our support for disability sports, to promote more participation and to set up a stronger pipeline for excellence.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I will say more about this when we launch the Disability Sports Master Plan (DSMP) next month, but let me sketch out a few key points.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have seen that time and time again, how important how sport is to participation, uplifting morale, giving us a sense of self-worth.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will therefore progressively enhance accessibility to public sports facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Persons with disabilities can look forward to ActiveSG gym orientation programmes that will be ready by later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But, Sir, inclusivity is more than just accessibility.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: More importantly, beyond just catering to accessibility, SportSG and their partners have introduced a range of programmes for persons with disabilities to themselves take part in sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Not just be at the venues, but take part in sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There must, therefore, be suitable programmes to encourage a stronger sense of participation and community.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The ActiveSG Para Sport Academy have also started programmes to provide persons with disabilities opportunities to participate in sports such as wheelchair rugby and para canoe.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY and SportSG have also embarked on efforts to step up on our plans leading into the DSMP.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Since last year, my colleague, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua has led a taskforce comprising various stakeholders to listen to ideas, to take on suggestions and to push the boundary and the envelope on how we can refresh the DSMP.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: More than 800 stakeholders have been engaged and they have provided us with very good ideas which we will take onboard.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will announce our recommendations to refresh the DSMP shortly.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will focus on more opportunities for persons with disabilities to participate in sports regularly, at the base level, having more participation and more opportunity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To also raise more awareness and to bring our community together, through unified participation like Play Inclusive, bringing able-bodied persons with persons with disabilities on the same team, taking part collectively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And also to have a clear pathway for sporting excellence as we nurture, cultivate and develop sporting talent for the next generation of disability sports excellence.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But if we pull in the same direction, work collectively, united, we can turn our size into an advantage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: NSAs, SportSG, SSI, NYSI, Singapore National Olympic Council (SNOC) and Singapore National Paralympics Council (SNPC) have to be cohesive and concerted in our efforts to advance sports together in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the same time, we will gradually step up professionalising the talent that we have in sports administration.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This overall will benefit our athletes as well as the support structure for our athletes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We build the base, we strengthen the pipeline, we invest in technical expertise in sports science, we professionalise our sports administration.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We need to find a way to bring this all together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have six strategies, but it is important that they work in tandem and they work cohesively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At the National Day Rally this year, the Prime Minister announced the Kallang Alive Masterplan.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is a bold and comprehensive plan to put sports firmly at the front our agenda, to create a clear pathway for success for Singaporeans through sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It will allow younger Singaporeans to choose sports first and be supported in their choice.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Kallang Alive plans will bring all our six strategies, coalescing them physically, literally under one roof.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will bring together athletes, sports science, NSA, coaches, officials and Sports School into our Home of Team Singapore, which will be in the middle of our Kallang Alive Masterplan.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: All of these wrapped around with dedicated, world-class training facilities, a National Training Centre with facilities for Para Sports, and an expanded sport science and sport medicine centre.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also more closely integrate with our sporting institutions and bring everyone together to inspire one another, leverage and build on economies of scale, inspire one another and to collectively call ourselves one Team Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As the Prime Minister announced, the whole of Singapore will also be a part of this experience in the Kallang Alive Precinct, with the activation of the beautiful Kallang Alive waterfront area as well as the pedestrianising of the boulevard running through the precinct.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also hoist in the lessons of their journeys and we do what we can to ensure that we will be better tomorrow than we were yesterday.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But with what we have, you have our commitment that we will continue to support our athletes and their aspirations as best we can.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To our Team Singapore athletes, we know how tough it is to be an athlete at this level, to be constantly challenged, to keep yourself always at the peak of your levels.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: You are constantly pushing the boundaries of your potential, chasing greatness with every training, with every competition, and with every moment of preparation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The journey is filled with challenges, but then again, it is these very challenges and obstacles that will sharpen your instinct and strengthen your resolve.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Remember that excellence is not just about talent.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is equally about discipline, resilience and the ability to rise again after every fall.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Stay focused, trust the process and embrace every opportunity to compete because each step forward is a victory in and of itself.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The Olympics and Paralympics are the epitome of all sporting competitions.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Badminton world champion, Loh Kean Yew, managed to reach the Men’s Singles quarter finals.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Swimmer, Gan Ching Hwee, set her personal bests and broke the National records for 800-metre and 1,500-metre freestyle.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Los Angeles 2028 Olympics will come around faster than we realise.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: To help our athletes unleash their fullest potential and excel at the Los Angeles 2028 and Brisbane 2032 Olympics, SportSG and respective NSAs must now begin to work closely with our athletes, coaches and parents.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: A world-class athlete starts training from an extremely early age.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Michael Phelps, the American swimmer and the most decorated Olympian of all times, with 28 Olympic medals, was only 19 when he won his first gold medals at Athens Olympics in 2004.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: More recently, diving sensation, Quan Hong Chan, was only 14 years old when she won a gold medal at Tokyo Olympics in 2021.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: At the Paris Olympics 2024, French Paddler, Felix Lebrun, 17 years old, won two bronze medals.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Our very own bronze medallist, Max Maeder, is also 17.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Our table tennis players, Izaac Quek and Zhou Jingyi, are respectively 18 and 19.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: They are also amongst the youngest Team Singapore athletes to have competed in the Paris Olympics.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The Singapore Sports School can be our critical gamechanger.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: From a young age, Joseph Schooling, our only Olympic gold medallist, took the non-mainstream pathway to study and train in the United States (US).

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Max Maeder is home-schooled and has to travel abroad very frequently to train and compete.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The question here is, even though the Sports School has managed to have churned out 19 Olympians, how soon can the school produce an Olympic medal winner?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: We are all aware that nothing is predictable but after 20 years of not being able to produce an Olympic medallist, we would need to take a critical look at the changes required.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: We must understand the unique challenges and constraints in our current system and adjust our current strategy.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: As a result, there is a shortfall of high-level competitions and our athletes would have to travel frequently or be based overseas to train and learn from the best athletes around the globe.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: While the Sports School has a very student-centric programme that works around their competition schedules, there is not such an academic programme in the higher institutes of learning.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Our national athletes would have to follow the same academic and attendance standards as their peers in our local polytechnics and universities.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: This stringent academic requirement becomes very challenging whenever they must travel overseas.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Their progress and sporting performance will invariably suffer a decline over the two years as they are unable to train and compete regularly.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: This enlistment period will inevitably coincide with the most crucial sporting peak years.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: First, we obviously must invest in world-class coaches with a track record of developing Olympians, be it an international or a Singaporean coach.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The coach works closely with the athlete on technical aspects, physical fitness and competition strategy.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The coach is the most crucial partner for an elite athlete and this is especially so during the formative years.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The athlete’s mental strength is critical for any personal breakthrough and is the defining factor between winning or losing.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: An experienced coach, and preferably once an Olympian, can better understand the intense psychological pressures and better prepare and strengthen the athletes’ mental resilience.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Most athletes in their teenage years are not ready for the pressure and limelight thrown upon professional sportsmen and sportswomen.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The coach is the mentor to guide and protect them from unnecessary pressures and distractions.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Though already at age 27, Shanti won the 200 metres gold and 100 metres silver medals at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: She has broken the national record for 100 metres and 200 metres multiple times.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Coach Cunha himself was a national sprinter and had represented Portugal at three Olympics Games.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Shanti credited her spectacular breakthrough to her coach, Cunha.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Former Olympian swimmer, Mark Chay, coached Paralympian swimmer, Yip Pin Xiu, since 2019 and she continues to fly the Singapore flag high.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Former Olympians and national table tennis head coaches Gao Ning and Jing Junhong trained Izaac Quek and Zhou Jingyi since their formative years in the Singapore Sports School.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I hope that SportSG and respective NSAs will continue to identify and attract the best coaches, especially those with Olympic experiences.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: NS is mandatory for all fit and eligible male Singaporeans and Permanent Residents, and there should be no exceptions.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Defence Minister, Dr Ng Eng Hen has also shared in Parliament in July 2022 that MINDEF is prepared to allow more national athletes to disrupt their full-time national service to train for international competitions.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The problem athletes face is that the deferment of NS duties till after the Olympics may in turn result in a deferment of the loss of critical training and competition window.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: As a result, the deferred NS duties may actually coincide with subsequent Olympics where the stakes may be even higher.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Thereafter, the athlete is being seconded to SportSG to complete the remaining NS term.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: During this period, the athlete must focus on full-time training and competition, in preparation for next Olympics Games.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: For his reservist, the athlete can also serve in SportSG if he is still actively competing.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: The time provided to them during the secondment period will be extremely critical for them to stay in top form, improve their international rankings needed to qualify for the next Olympic Games and hone their mental resilience for the battles ahead.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Competition at the highest level is relentless and the window of opportunity is extremely short.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: As a nation, we should be giving our top athletes the maximum resources and clear the roadblocks for them, so that they can go all out without reservations, to compete against their opponents on the global sporting arenas.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: We should not only be spending top dollars to build world-class infrastructure and sending our athletes for multiple training stints and competitions overseas.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: We must be laser-sharp in our focus on how our athletes may achieve their full sporting potential and help them.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: If our system does not provide maximum support to our top athletes, then we should not expect anything more from sports other than healthy living.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I hope the MCCY and MINDEF will consider my two suggestions.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: As a nation, we must be realistic and realise that our full support to all our athletes, coaches and Team Singapore officials, determines how our athletes will fare in sports.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This extends, of course, to our most recent medallists in Paris: Jeralyn Tan and Max Maeder, as well as Yip Pin Xiu, our country's most decorated sportsperson.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: All of us that have played sport will understand the enormous sacrifices and challenges that athletes had to endure to climb the pinnacle of sporting achievement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Their feats would not have been possible without years of gruelling dedication to their chosen sport, culminating in translating those countless hours into a competition-day delivery, that would have had to be one of the best in their lives.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This was undoubtedly the case for Jeralyn, Pin Xiu and Max, after which this Motion has specifically named.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Jeralyn had trailed by five points at the halfway mark, but was able to muster a fierce comeback that forced a tie-breaker in the final round.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It was her enormous composure and mental prowess in the face of tough odds that led us to our first Paralympic boccia medal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Kitefoiler Max had to overcome a somewhat slow start in the first race of the final to pull into second place, but it was his steady consistency in the face of poor weather conditions during the finals that saw him ultimately snatch a place on the podium.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In doing so, he tacked and jibed his way into history as our nation's youngest Olympic medallist – and of course, into our hearts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And Pin Xiu displayed her usual fortitude, not allowing the complacency of being the world record holder or already having won gold twice in the 100-metre backstroke to faze her, as she clocked a historic three-peat that saw her taking home a gold on the second day of the Games, followed by another two days later, in the 50-metre backstroke.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: To them, and all the others here that have carried our flag, we celebrate and honour your immense physical and mental strength that have led to your wonderful accomplishments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Without diminishing the passion and hard work that have driven our athletes to their sporting success, I would like to share some thoughts about how we reward them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Questions of this nature are not unique to me, of course.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The People's Action Party and Workers' Party (WP) Members of Parliament had previously asked questions about the seemingly unequal rewards and recognition accorded to both athletes, with and without disabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is clearly a matter of bipartisan concern.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This response was essentially repeated by Minister Tong's response to previous Parliamentary Questions that have been filed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But are they, indeed, NGOs of the same standing and milieu as, say, the Association of Women for Action and Research (AWARE), Sayoni, or the Humanitarian Organization for Migration Economics (HOME)?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The SNOC was established to receive the official invitation by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) to send Singaporean representatives to the Games.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The current president of the SNOC is Minister Grace Fu, and past presidents and council members include Ministers and Members of Parliament.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The SNPC has similar language describing the primary sponsor of the AAA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The Tote Board is a Government agency, and its activities, and those of its subsidiary entities, are regulated by various Ministries.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, if the Government does choose to exercise greater influence over the MGA and AAA, the question that remains is whether the current amounts granted in each are reasonable from an economic and moral perspective.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: What should the value of such an award be?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Some have claimed that we ought to respect the economics of supply and demand.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While I do not believe, ironically enough, that economics should be the basis for justifying such rewards, allow me to elaborate on why such arguments are somewhat naive.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The supply side is straightforward: this is the effort expended by our sportsmen and women that compete in major international games.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But as any athlete will tell you, their driving motivation to perform at their best in the sporting arena often has very little to do with monetary gains.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Indeed, most do it for their deep love for the game and would almost certainly do it for comparatively little money.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: And the fact that so many of our athletes do so, for generally low levels of remuneration, is a living testament to that reality.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Many have put their lives on hold to bring glory to the nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Still, there is no denying that even our leanest and meanest athletes need to eat, drink and earn a living.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: At the margin, rewards for performance at the highest levels do make a difference in ensuring that our sportsmen and women are able to continue the pursuit of their passion, not least by allowing them to persist in the rigours of their training and climbing the ladder of competition during the lean years, where success is neither assured nor yet guaranteed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In contrast, demand derives from us, the audience and supporters and lovers of a sport.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Our interest – and willingness, to pay for the joy and entertainment we receive when we watch sporting events – is what allows a sport, any sport, to be viable enough that professionals can emerge.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It is along these lines that some have chosen to argue that the comparative lack of demand for the Paralympics means that there is little economic justification to rewarding Paralympians with the same order of monetary compensation as our Olympians, when they medal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Here is the problem with such an argument.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: While such dynamics may be true for any sport as a whole, it seldom translates into actual compensation for individual sportsmen and women.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: After all, raw market forces have seldom been the sole driver for monetary compensation in sport.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If so, the US' women's soccer team – which both draws far larger crowds and generates significantly larger revenue, at least within the US, and has in fact, achieved much greater sporting success than the men's team – would not have filed suit against its own soccer federation for reasons of unequal pay.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Nor would the athletes playing in the billion-dollar National Collegiate Athletic Association leagues continue to receive only limited compensation, in the form of tuition waivers, living expenses and endorsement rights.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Let us take such an argument to its logical conclusion.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But we do not, and rightly so; we recognise that we wish to support a wide range of sport, because we see the value in each one and every one of them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Rather, salaries and rewards in sport are determined as much by sponsorship interest, relative bargaining power and the institutional strictures, much like the payouts for the MGA and AAA are.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But it is worth, perhaps, exploring the moral arguments, which I believe are even more compelling.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Hence, another argument sometimes made to justify the differential rewards that Paralympians compete in finer categories; subsequently, their field of competition is correspondingly smaller and hence, they deserve less of a reward for rising to the top of that narrowed field.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: To me, this is, again, a distinction without a difference.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Fields widen and narrow every year, for all sorts of reasons.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Birth cohorts fall in size in certain Chinese horoscope years and rise in others, but we do not tell those who were born in the year of the Dragon that their "A" Division golds somehow deserve more acclaim than those who had won in other years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Similarly, we do not tell our female weightlifters and bodybuilders that, because their sport is less popular among women than it is with men, or that more bodyweight categories exist in one gender versus the other, they should receive a smaller reward when they win.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Rather, our awards are simply organised by the coverage of the competition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This approach is defensible, because it does not prescribe, in advance, whether any given sport or athlete should be deemed more worthy of a greater reward, based on their observable attributes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Instead, it focuses, as it should, on how many potential competitors there might be, based on the geographic scope of the competition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This argument also glosses over the fact that what the different categories capture are disabilities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Lest we forget, Paralympians placed in these different categories are competing not on the basis of these classifications, but in spite of them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Hence, I personally find any suggestion that the athlete is somehow, even if indirectly, benefiting from this smaller field morally indefensible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But life, of course, is about much more than that.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I will conclude by explaining why equality in monetary rewards for sport implies something that goes well beyond the pecuniary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Certainly, our country recognises and celebrates the achievements of our Paralympians in many ways beyond the financial.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But, in my view, not only are such accolades insufficient, they also strike me as inconsistent.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If these non-pecuniary benefits alone were sufficient, then surely no additional MGA or AAA would be necessary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Conversely, if we see the value to a monetary reward of even a single dollar, then it behoves us to explain why we are comfortable with a distinction between our able-bodied versus disabled sports people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I believe that this Government, as a key stakeholder in the IOC, as the controlling body of the Tote Board and as the elected leaders of our people and society, can make the call to do so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: We should not defer the decision to other bodies with less standing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Other countries have also taken steps to move toward parity between the two.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: We routinely argue in this House about ensuring equal opportunities for every Singaporean.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: We have repeatedly spoken about fostering a society of compassion and empathy and we await the passage in this House on the Non-Discrimination Bill, an idea that the WP has championed for a long time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Let us do so with the MGA and the AAA too, recognising the accomplishments of all our sportsmen and sportswomen equally, with the rewards that they so definitively deserve.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: From my school days to university and beyond, it has shaped who I am.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In secondary school, I was part of the school's gymnastics team.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In junior college, I competed in canoeing and dragon boating.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They taught me resilience, teamwork and determination, values that our Team Singapore, Olympians and Paralympians embody today.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As a former sportsperson and teacher, I have had the opportunity to understand sports from the inside out.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While studying sports science at Loughborough University, a leading sports institution, I saw first-hand, the grit required to compete at the very elite level.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I still remember those freezing winter mornings, waking up at 4.00 am and working as a lifeguard, watching national-level swimmers push through endless laps until 8.00 am, only to head straight to class.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Later, they would return for another training session in the evening.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: That level of commitment is something I see mirrored in our athletes back home.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In Singapore, I have had the privilege of closely observing our national canoeing team.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Their schedule is just as demanding, training many times a week, often with two sessions a day.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Their spirit is unyielding, their pursuit of excellence is relentless.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our athletes possess a unique drive, persistent to a fault and talented beyond measure.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For many of our athletes, the pursuit of excellence means setting aside tertiary education, stable careers and even long-term financial security.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These sacrifices are not always visible behind the shine of medals, but they are real and they deserve our recognition and support.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Support for our athletes has grown over the years.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Today, organisations, like the SSI and NYSI, form the backbone in nurturing and supporting our aspiring athletes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The mental well-being of our athletes deserves our attention, not just as they strive for victory but also as they transition into their post-sport careers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This can be a particularly vulnerable time and we must ensure that support systems are in place to navigate this change.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Do we currently offer a dedicated space where athletes in their post-sport careers can connect, share experiences and contribute their insights to shape future sporting policies?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Creating such a community could be invaluable, both in safeguarding their mental health and in harnessing their expertise for the betterment of sports in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This would demonstrate a genuine commitment to their overall well-being, beyond the medals and accolades.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The private sector has also played a role.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Contributions from the Tote Board and sponsorships for the Major Games Awards Programmes highlight that supporting our athletes is a shared responsibility.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It reminds us that our athletes are not alone on this journey.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am heartened that Singapore has taken further steps to support our sports community.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The spexEducation Undergraduate Scholarship guarantees that their education remains a priority.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: CPF top-ups for spexScholars ensure their future, housing, healthcare and retirement remains secure, even as they pursue their dreams.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Initiatives to make universities and workplaces more athlete-friendly further ease their path.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Additionally, we must also consider greater accessibility in training facilities for our para athletes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They face unique challenges and often have to rise above societal expectations, facing obstacles beyond those of their able-bodied peers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Enhanced access to facilities can ensure that they too, have an environment that nurtures their talents and supports their pursuit of excellence.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is a dedicated space where our athletes can train, study and live.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: By integrating the relocated sports school into this campus, we are creating an ideal environment for our athletes to thrive.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is a commitment to their daily grind and their highest ambitions, a signal that sports can be a viable career.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: These efforts matter because our athletes do more than just compete.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Their achievements unite us, reminding us of what is possible when we push beyond our limits.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They embody resilience and instill a sense of national pride that goes beyond medals.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, we must acknowledge that these initiatives require significant resources and we must be strategic with our investments.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Government should prioritise support for athletes and sports that deliver the greatest return for Singapore, whether that is through national unity or international acclaim.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This approach, while potentially leading to varying levels of support across different sports, encourages our NSAs to strive for excellence, broaden their reach and inspire greater participation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Yet, I understand that this perspective may raise concerns.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some may question if this means focusing less on sports like football, which has traditionally seen significant investment but has faced some challenges in delivering results.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But we should not overlook the deep connection many Singaporeans have with sports, like football, and its power to inspire unity and community spirit.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Thus, with any approach, we must balance the goal of strategic investments with the broader value that sports bring to our society.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: By focusing our resources thoughtfully, we can maximise the positive impact of sports on our nation, ensuring that all Singaporeans, regardless of their sporting passion, feel a sense of pride and inspiration.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It requires the entire ecosystem, from parents and coaches who nurture talent at a young age to the Government and private sector providing financial backing and to the community cheering them on at every step.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Let us honour not just the triumphs of our Team Singapore Olympians and Paralympians, but also the sacrifices and dedication that fuel their success.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Let us remember that behind every medal is a story of resilience, perseverance and national pride.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our athletes inspire us, unite us and remind us of the power of dreams.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is our duty to stand by them, not just in moments of victory but throughout their journey.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This means investing in their future, ensuring their well-being and celebrating their efforts, win or lose.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I call on this House to rally behind our athletes, not just with words of appreciation but with a sustained commitment to their growth and success.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Let us build a Singapore where every aspiring athlete knows that they have a nation behind them supporting their dreams and cheering them on.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: With that, I wholeheartedly support this Motion and urge all of us to be unwavering champions for those who wear the flag on their chest with pride.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am sure the whole House will agree with me that success is not defined solely by the medals our athletes and para athletes have won.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is defined by their courage to step up, their tenacity to compete and their grace to both celebrate victories and confront setbacks.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Our Team Singapore athletes have shown exemplary dedication, perseverance, resilience and commitment to their sports.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The medal is a crowning achievement for her long career in boccia.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: She has worked hard at the sport since 2008 when she picked it up at the Cerebral Palsy Alliance Singapore School.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: He showed us skill, agility and calm under pressure against the world's best at the kitefoiling finals.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These are qualities that will undoubtedly serve him well as he continues to rise in the sport.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Since the Olympics, he has already gone on to clinch three championships in a row.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We look forward to witnessing further sporting success from him in the coming years.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Her achievements have inspired a nation and raised the profile of disabled athletes in our country.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: She has demonstrated that with hard work and determination, Singaporeans can excel globally and her success reminds us that there is no limit to what can be achieved when one dares to dream.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As we celebrate the achievements of our Olympians and Paralympians, I hope the House will also join me in recognising the tireless efforts of the coaches, support staff and families who have contributed to their success.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, on behalf of PSP, I would like to congratulate our Team Singapore Olympians and Paralympians for their outstanding achievements at the 2024 Paris Olympic and Paralympic Games.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: They exemplify the spirit of tenacity and the grace to both celebrate victories and confront setbacks.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Their participation in the Games has inspired an entire nation and showcased the best of the Singapore spirit – courage, discipline and teamwork.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Here, I would like to pay my highest tribute to Team Singapore.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This year, we are also proud to recognise three medallists, Jeralyn Tan, Maximilian Maeder and Yip Pin Xiu.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Ms Jeralyn Tan has devoted many years to Boccia and did very well at this year's Paralympics by clinching Singapore's first medal in Boccia.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Maximilian Maeder achieved a bronze medal in kitefoiling at just 17 years of age and he will have a bright future in this sport.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: She is also the world record holder for both of these events, making her one of the most outstanding performers in Paralympics.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Meanwhile, we also recognise the tireless efforts of the coaches, support staff and families behind the scenes, without which Team Singapore's success would not have been possible. : Sir, the 2024 Paris Olympic and Paralympic Games have left an indelible mark on our nation.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Let us continue to support our athletes, nurture their talent and build a sporting culture that empowers every Singaporean to dream big and pursue excellence.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: By giving your best in Paris, you have made our nation proud, and we look forward to your future endeavours with great excitement and confidence.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: May your success continue to inspire Singaporeans across generations.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The achievements bear testament to our athletes’ dedication and hard work.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: As important, the achievements also bear testament to the committed long-term support for Team Singapore athletes from different quarters of society.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Such committed long-term support is no different from the concept of patient capital, a transformative approach to impact investing.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Their successes inspire younger Singaporeans to hold fast to sporting ambitions.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
