text: As a society, how might we raise the patient capital needed to build on 2024’s achievements and to give courage to more Singaporeans to commit to representing Singapore in sports at the international level?

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: In response, I call on more of us to recognise that the value of sporting excellence is lasting and wide-reaching and to acknowledge that there is a price to the process of achieving sporting excellence.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The former, of recognising the value of sporting excellence, manifests itself in the visible pride that we have for our Olympians and Paralympians.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: We followed the Games and cheered them on as they took to the stage.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: We are proud of our Team Singapore athletes and their efforts.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The latter, of acknowledging that there is a price to achieve sporting excellence, requires us to adopt the mindframe of patient capital: think long term and impact-seeking.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The decision to invest in athlete development and, in turn, sporting excellence, should not be solely dictated by what is tangible and measurable.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The Minister shared about Sport Singapore and various NSAs making concerted efforts to spot athletes at a younger age to provide them a longer runway to train and compete at a high-performance level.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Nevertheless, we must respect the fact that progress takes time, and every athlete develops and peaks at a different pace.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Therein lies the need to reconcile society’s orientation on goals and medals with the long-term horizon necessary for athlete development and success.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The first C: corporates that step up to the plate.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Corporates, too, can communicate their support for our athletes’ longer-term development by pledging longer-term funding to the One Team Singapore Fund.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Doing so would, especially, give a leg-up to athletes from emerging sports that might be more challenged in fund-raising than established and popular sports and yet would require more support and resources to achieve breakthrough performances.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Providing greater transparency in the utilisation of the One Team Singapore Fund could encourage more corporates to step up to the plate as impact outcomes become more visible.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The second C: coaches who are committed to longer-term athlete development.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: I represent freelance coaches and instructors in my capacity as the Executive Secretary of the National Instructors and Coaches Association (NICA).

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Many of our NICA members are sports coaches who deliver sports CCAs to public schools.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: I have fond memories of my involvement in various sport CCAs, thanks to supportive and caring coaches who challenged me to think and go beyond my self-imposed limitations.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The experience has shaped my life outlook and reinforced the grit, resilience and fortitude that I draw upon to navigate life challenges.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: For our athletes to yield outsized impact, patient capital must extend to supporting those who nurture the seeds of sporting aspiration in our younger generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Many sports coaches have shared with NICA their concerns about schools reducing CCA hours and seeking to taper down the competitive element in CCAs.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: They have also shared concerns about the challenges of eking out a career as a professional sports coach in Singapore because of dampening school demand and increased compliance costs.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Behind every successful athlete stands a committed professional sports coach.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: I would suggest a review of the support to coaches and coaches’ livelihood as part of strengthening the ecosystem of support for athlete development.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: NICA stands ready to contribute to the review.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The third C: contributions of athletes are valued by society.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: We live in a practical society where success is often measured by achievements.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Every athlete must develop a winning mindset and approach.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: However, athletes might not consistently yield medal wins as the fruits of labour.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: The glare of the practical society can be unforgiving and beset athletes with worry and stress.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: What Prime Minister Lawrence Wong shared at his speech at the Institute of Policy Studies' 35th anniversary conference in 2023 is instructive.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: He said: “We must provide many more ways for our diverse talents to be the best possible version of themselves, to make a difference in their own ways, all deserving of equal respect in our society”.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: More can be done to communicate to our athletes that their contributions are valued, beyond the sport and as part of the larger society.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Marcel Proust, the early 20th century French novelist, wrote: “Let us be grateful to the people who make us happy; they are the charming gardeners who make our souls blossom.” There is a price to the process of achieving sporting excellence.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Our athletes have given their all to their calling.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Their successes and achievements at the international arenas have inspired and energised us.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: Through them, we are united as One Team Singapore.

speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
text: It now lies upon us, as members of Team Singapore, to be the charming gardeners to our athletes.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Our athletes give us so much more than just medals.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: They show us what it is like to perform under pressure and to work hard at a goal.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: When they succeed, the whole country unites behind them and cheers.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: And when they do not, we are privileged to be able to witness a masterclass in courage, grace and strength, as we watch them recover from their setbacks.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Our medallists have done incredibly well and every single Olympian and Paralympian who made it to the Games this year is a winner in my eyes.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: In support of this Motion, I would like to make three points.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: The Paris Olympic Games saw about 11,040 athletes from all over the world taking part in 32 sports; and the Paralympic Games saw around 4,400 athletes competing in 22 individual and team sports.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Coming from a tiny country like Singapore, the act of even qualifying for a spot in the Games is a momentous achievement.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: On this point, I hope that athletes and para athletes can be rewarded more for the act of qualification.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: This could take the form of better profiling and publicity to encourage private sponsorship, or better outright cash awards and allowances.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: CNBC Sport recently, on 29 August, published an article entitled "Here’s how much athletes at the Paris Paralympics earn for winning medals".

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: The article, which is self-explanatory from its title, set out a list of how much para athletes are awarded by different countries when they win medals.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore was at the top of a league table of 13 countries, which is a fantastic achievement, but the article also noted that countries like Spain, Canada, France, Australia and South Korea were offering Paralympic medallists rewards that were equal to that of their Olympic counterparts.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: The article continued that Hong Kong and Singapore, which award the largest payouts to their Olympic medallists, still do not give out as much to their Paralympic victors.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: I acknowledge that there was an increase in awards for our Paralympians in in 2021 and 2022.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: I know this issue has been raised multiple times in this House by many Members, as well as by activist groups outside the House, but I would nonetheless still like to add my voice to the call for parity in the awards for our Olympians and Paralympians.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: I understand that these are decisions made by the SNOC and SNPC.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: These are non-government organisations, of course, and I am also aware that there is a long history to how these monetary awards were created, developed over time and funded.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: However, I would like to highlight that it is also stated on the SNOC website that the Tote Board family, comprising the Tote Board, Singapore Pools and the Singapore Turf Club, is the primary sponsor of the SNOC MAP.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: The Tote Board is also publicly listed as one of the two primary sponsors of the AAA.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Of course, post-podium rewards should be paired with holistic efforts to support our athletes in their journey to the podium – one should not come at the expense of the other and it should also not be the case that the two are mutually exclusive.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: That being said, financial awards do have an important role to play.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: There is plenty of data on this, I will just highlight one research study today.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: This was published in 2020, in the journal Frontiers in Psychology.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: It was found in that report that when appropriately applied, financial awards can increase confidence, achievement motivation, coachability, goal setting and mental preparation for athletes.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: In this particular study, football players who were awarded financial incentives generally showed better performance when compared to non-awarded players.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: More importantly though, cash awards also have a signalling effect.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: In this year’s Committee of Supply (COS) debates I advocated for cash awards for our Cultural Medallion winners and there are many parallels between sports and the arts scene in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Our artists and sportspeople sacrifice a great deal to take the path less travelled.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Both the arts and sports play an important role in creating national identity and in making Singapore a distinctive home for us all.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: In a similar vein to what I said in the COS debates, cash awards will signal accomplishment and prestige, recognising the life achievements of our country’s best sportspeople.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: They will inspire others to embark on similar paths, and further encourage those who are already on the journey to sporting greatness.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Awarding our athletes and para athletes with the same top prizes sends a powerful message of inclusion.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: One that tells our society and the world that we value both sets of athletes equally.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: At the moment, a grant may be brought to tax depending on factors such as whether the awardee is carrying on a trade, business, profession or vocation in relation to their sporting ability, or whether they are an employee of a sports body.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: This status can change within the course of a single year as well.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: In these situations, a detailed assessment on tax liability would have to take place on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: An exemption would not would only reduce administrative and compliance burdens on both the tax authority and taxpayers, but it would also send a clear message that these specific awards are granted as a pure reward for the recipients as a prize for a lifetime of their hard work.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: Successful professional sportspeople would still be brought to tax on their other earnings from private sponsorships and endorsements.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: It is not the case that once the funds are rewarded, that is the end of the story and there is no return to society.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: So, we need to ask ourselves, do we really need to impose an additional layer of tax on top of these awards and winnings.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: I note the Minister's comment when he moved this Motion that we do not have unlimited resources in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
text: But I would, nonetheless, ask him and MOF to consider this suggestion.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Today, we celebrate the successes of our national athletes, in particular Ms Jeralyn Tan, Mr Maximilian Maeder and Ms Yip Pin Xiu, who have brought immense honour to Singapore on the world stage.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: To Jeralyn, Max, and Pin Xiu: your dedication, resilience, and sporting excellence were on full display in Paris.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: You have inspired all of us who were rooting for you at home.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Before the Paris Games, “kitefoiling” was not a term that most Singaporeans have even heard of.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Yet, after Max brought home the Olympic bronze, we have seen couch experts springing up all over the island, eager to discuss this exciting sport they have always known and loved.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Max may seem like an overnight success, but this cannot be further from the truth.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: His well-documented story tells of a boy who started honing his skills and competing at the young age of 11.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: At 18, Max is already a decorated athlete and a household name.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Max, you deserve all the flowers and we wish you many more fantastic years ahead.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Pin Xiu and Jeralyn, I extend my heartfelt congratulations to you, on your remarkable triumph of the human spirit.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: But many may not know, just two months before that, Jeralyn had to endure a heartbreaking quarter final elimination from the World Boccia Cup in Portugal.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: While others may have crumbled under a disappointment of this scale, Jeralyn demonstrated her never-say-die attitude and has now etched her name in the history books.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Her strength in the face of adversity is a testament to her character and this must not go unrecognised.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: As for Pin Xiu, welcome back, you are no stranger to this House and to sporting glory.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I remember watching the 100m backstroke event and was incredulous when I realised that Pin Xiu won the event by a margin of 0.06 seconds.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Even the commentators could not tell who won, in real-time.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Pin Xiu, it must have been an exhilarating race for you.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: In my younger days, I took part in amateur swimming competitions run by the Singapore Disability Sports Council (SDSC).

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: In the pool, I imagined representing and winning a medal for Singapore at the Paralympics.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: As you can see, that remains a dream I had not fulfilled.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: While we applaud our medal winners, let us not forget all our Team Singapore athletes who competed at the highest level.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: We see your sacrifices, your grit and your unwavering dedication to representing our nation with pride.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: You have given your all, and your pursuit of excellence is something we all deeply admire and respect.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: I hope you do not forget to celebrate as well, for you have truly earned it.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: To those who supported our athletes – family and friends, performance coaches, sports scientists, psychologists, doctors and many more – your role is just as vital.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: We recognise you too, for your contributions behind the scenes have been crucial in unlocking the potential of our sporting champions.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: It is an inclusive force that can unite a nation.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Our national athletes show us what is possible if you take sporting talent and ambition to the next level.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: But what about the rest of us, those who play sports socially, recreationally, or just to stay fit?

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Beyond improving one’s physical health, participating in sports also builds discipline and boosts self-confidence.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: It can reduce stress, prevent cognitive decline and combat depression.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: In short, sports participation materially improves our quality of life.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: This is even more so for persons with disabilities, as engaging in sports can enhance mobility, foster independence and build resilience.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Inclusive sports participation is therefore essential to ensure that persons with disabilities feel welcomed, so that they too can reap the benefits of sports.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: To make sports truly inclusive, it will take a whole-of-society approach.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: The Government, everyday Singaporeans, caregivers and persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: All three groups have a crucial role to play.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: First, it is vital for the Government to keep inclusive programming at the heart of policy-making, to encourage more to participate.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: For example, in mainstream schools, are we doing enough to include children with disabilities in physical education classes?

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Unlike their peers in SPED schools, students with disabilities in mainstream settings do not have a structured approach to sports participation.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: We need to do more to ensure that persons with disabilities are exposed to sports and its benefits at a young age, to give them a higher shot of sustaining sports participation later in life.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Building more accessible infrastructure alone is not enough.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: There is an urgent need to do much better in how we raise awareness and promote the benefits of sports.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: As we look forward to the update of the DSMP – and I thank Minister Edwin Tong for earlier giving us a glimpse of what to expect – it is critical to ensure that persons with disabilities and their caregivers fully embrace all that sports can offer.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Second, everyday Singaporeans have a part to play too.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: When you see someone who looks different from you, do you stare, or do you recognise them as part of your larger community?

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Simple gestures, like a warm smile, offering a seat, and other acts of kindness can go a long way.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: If each of us makes an effort to foster inclusive and accepting environments, more persons with disabilities will feel comfortable to show up, participate, and thrive in our shared spaces.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: And third, all of this will remain an academic discussion if persons with disabilities and their caregivers do not, themselves, take the first step to participate.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: For those unsure of where to begin, setting personal goals can be a great way to get yourself motivated.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: These goals do not need to be grand or lofty.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Sometimes, achieving the goal of being able to get out of bed independently, can be a rewarding and significant milestone.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: And from there, who knows where that progress will take you?

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: Whether you choose to turn therapy into a competitive career is completely up to you.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: If not, taking part in sports simply to stay fit, make friends, and enjoy yourself is just as valuable.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: In closing, I wish to once again, extend my warmest congratulations to our Team Singapore athletes for their outstanding achievements.

speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
text: By carrying the torch and blazing the way forward, you set an inspiring example for us all to reach for greater heights, and shape the Singapore we want to live in.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It gives me great joy to come together to celebrate the incredible achievements of Team Singapore at the 2024 Paris Olympic and Paralympic Games.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The 33 athletes who represented our nation have demonstrated the spirit of resilience, resolve and excellence, carrying our Singapore flag high on the world state.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Pin Xiu, serves with me in the Purple Parade movement, which sees thousands of Singaporeans coming together each year to show their support for the cause of inclusion and for the disability community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We sat in many meetings together and what impresses me most is her humility, authenticity and her willingness to constantly learn, not just in swimming, but in other things, in leadership issues and advocacy and so forth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I know Pin Xiu will go far as a woman of substance in life.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But beyond the medals, it is so important that we recognise every athlete who participated in the Games, whether they reached the podium or not.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They, on the road to Paris, they demonstrated the triumph of the human spirit, all 33 of you.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: None of this success would be possible without the strong support system behind each athlete.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, to the families, thank you for releasing and supporting the athletes to take this road less travelled.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I salute you and you are as special as the athletes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: To the coaches and the leaders and the staff of the NSAs, the Disability Sports Council, the sports institutes who tirelessly train and guide our athletes, ensuring that they perform at their best, your contributions have been invaluable.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, thank you all, members of this important support structure, for being the wind below the wings of our athletes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I also want to express my gratitude to the Singapore Government as well and I want to give credit where it is due.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Over the years, the Government has increased its investment in sports, not just in terms of infrastructure and funding, but also in terms of trying to build a more inclusive sporting culture.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Our para athletes' achievements have shown us that sports is not just a domain of the so-called able-bodied.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The Government's inclusive sports investment has enabled both mainstream and Paralympic athletes to receive the support that they need to succeed on the world stage.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Indeed, when I asked Pin Xiu what had been a game-changer for her swimming career, she mentioned the support she got from the support system, from being able to have access to the right coach and a high-quality sports science team.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The success we are witnessing today is a direct result of this intentional upstream investment and we look forward to seeing even more growth in the years to come.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Next, let me now share a few areas I got feedback from past Olympians, their families and a few other athletes on where we feel Singapore has done well in developing sports talent and also areas that we can do even better.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: What Singapore has done well in developing sports talent.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The Singapore sports team has grown tremendously, especially in recent years and we have made significant progress in developing sports talent, both in mainstream and disability sports.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The establishment of the Singapore Sports Hub and other regional training centres has provided our athletes with the platforms they need to participate and then to excel.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The announcement by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Minister Edwin Tong on the new home of Team Singapore in the Kallang Alive precinct presents an exciting vision.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The second thing we have done well, is also for support for our athlete development.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Through initiatives, like spex, many of my colleagues have mentioned before, spexProgramme and so forth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We are seeing greater financial and developmental support for our athletes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: SpexScholarships, in particular, have helped many of our athletes focus on their sports full-time while also pursuing their education or career.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Singapore has also made great strides in identifying and nurturing young talent through schools, clubs and national age group competitions.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Programmes, such as the NYSI, have played a crucial role in grooming the next generation of sporting stars by providing specialised training and education support for our student athletes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One of the areas where Singapore has improved tremendously is the promotion of inclusive sports.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Thanks to MCCY and the team, the introduction of more robust support structures for our Paralympic athletes, including dedicated training programmes and specialised coaching, has allowed them to compete at the highest level.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Disability sports have seen greater attention, greater funding, creating more opportunities for athletes with disabilities to develop their talent.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is, therefore, welcome news that the new home of Team Singapore, I mentioned just now, will have a dedicated training centre for para sports.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I am also very pleased that a review of the 2016 DSMP, I think overdue, now led by the Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua, is now underway to further improve sports access for persons with disabilities, young and old, and I look forward to the Master Plans addressing ground aspirations, such as a bigger network of sports coaches, facilities and programmes also for adults with disabilities to participate and even excel in sports.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: While we have achieved much, I think there are still areas where we need to do a little bit more.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In broadening sports participation in schools and mainstream schools, although we have offered more opportunities, we should offer more opportunities for students of all skills level, not only those who are proficient.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We must also facilitate further the integration of sports into the curriculum at special schools to ensure that children with disabilities, especially those with higher support needs, are encouraged to lead healthy, active lives from a young age.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many of the special education (SPED) school graduates still do not.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Not enough of them have adopted healthy lifestyles when they exit school.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This has to be intentional and has to go beyond a few lessons a week.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: More structured opportunities, both within the schools and out there, with the grassroots and the community, are needed.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: By fostering early sports participation, we can instill healthy habits that extend into adulthood, enriching the overall quality of life, reducing healthcare concerns and costs and potentially producing more elite athletes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Next, on equalising cash rewards – it seems to be a popular topic today.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Hot off the press, Paralympians Yip Pin Xiu and Jeralyn Tan have been rewarded this week for their outstanding achievements at the Paris Games.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For context, there are two distinct cash award schemes, the MAP for Olympians and the AAA for Paralympians.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Both programmes have different origins, different scopes and administration managed by separate NGOs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This is because I know, for so many years, how my fellow disability advocates and I have been asking the Government and sponsors and foundations to give us more grants, more funds, for more services for the disabled, especially for the adult years from 21 to, say, 85.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In lifelong learning, we need funds in job support for persons with disabilities who can take on paid jobs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For those who cannot work or cannot take on paid jobs for care services, there is so much needed.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Caregiving services as well; in housing; in healthcare; in transport; criminal justice; and, for example, beefing up the Police force who are supporting our possible criminals with special needs; in mental wellness; in Healthier SG for all.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These are all services and areas that we need a lot more support and the needs are many.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Together, we can send a powerful and progressive message that Singapore is truly inclusive and we offer equal opportunities to all regardless of background.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, those are my views on parity of awards.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I know it is important in today's topic context to fight for parity.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But I also want to express that in the larger context, there are also many, many needs and I do want the Government to look at these needs as well and to spend as prudently as possible to ensure that more needs for more for the disabled can be looked into.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The next is on sports science and technology.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One area that we can improve on is by increasing investment in sports science and technology to help athletes maximise their performance through improved training methodologies and performance analytics.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Surely, younger athletes can be also connected with experienced mentors and even former Olympians to provide guidance, provide motivation and practical advice to them.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And finally, a very important area or topic.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: As I speak to past Olympian athletes, whether able-bodied or Paralympians, many of them have mentioned the area of post-career support for athletes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The transition from a sports career to life after competition can be daunting for many athletes, particularly for those who have devoted their youth to training.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These are the few areas that I would like MCCY to consider further.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And lastly, I just want to, again, congratulate all our remarkable athletes who represented Singapore at the 2024 Paris Olympic and Paralympic Games.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: You have made us so proud, not only with your victories but inspired, like what Minister Edwin Tong has said, your passion, your determination and the grit you have shown in every step of the way.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: A special congratulations and big thanks, too, to the incredible families, coaches, professionals who form the backbone of support.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Your unwavering belief in our athletes made all the difference.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: As we look to the future, let us dream even bigger.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: May the Singapore sports fraternity continue to grow from strength to strength.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: May you forge new paths of success, not just on the world stage but in every school, every neighbourhood, every community across our nation.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: May we build on this powerful legacy and create a future where sports is not just a field of competition but a celebration of Singapore's spirit of excellence, inclusivity and unity.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Let the world see what a great country we are and what we are further capable of.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, Majulah Singapura, thank you very much and congratulations.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: And along with my fellow Members, I would also like to add my congratulations to Team Singapore at the recent Olympics and the recent Paralympics.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Your collective performance encourages all of us to pursue excellence in sports as a national agenda.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: These would begin at our special needs education institutions and schools, and services for persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Our current curriculum may need to be expanded to facilitate, encourage and broaden interest and participation in sports.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: My colleagues, Mr Ong Hua Han and Ms Denise Phua have already spoken on this.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Selection of the type of sports will require appropriate counsel.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: We already have many helpful lessons from our Paralympians and their families.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Thirdly, we have many established social service providers who are providing support for persons with special needs and disabilities.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, larger funders, such as Tote Board – I know they are already helping in a great way – can help to supplement public funding, as will the private and people philanthropic and business communities.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In a conversation I had with one of our Paralympians, he called for more private sector sponsorship and support.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I hope more companies will see this as an avenue to support, thus enabling our current para athletes and future Paralympians to excel both locally and internationally.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: As we head towards a more inclusive society, let us also intentionally allocate increased public, private and people resources to strengthen and support our para athletes, current and future Paralympians, making suitable sports options more widely available and accessible.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Congratulations again to our Team Singapore Olympians and Paralympians!

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Our medallists have shown us what it means to embody the spirit of perseverance, passion and determination.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Their victories are not just personal triumphs, but also testaments to the values we hold dear as a nation – resilience, hard work and the will to rise above challenges.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Their success is not only a reflection of their talent and dedication, but also speaks of an unwavering support system that surrounds them, a system that embraces the individual while fostering a deep sense of collective identity and purpose.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: It is a vision, a vision of universal support, a vision of unity and a vision where every Singaporean, whether an aspiring Olympian or a weekend athlete, can find their potential fully realised.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Izaac Quek, Singapore's youngest local-born table tennis player to qualify for the Olympics, provides a glimpse of how Home of Team Singapore is already taking shape.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: His Olympic quest in table tennis is supported by a personal education pathway at the Singapore Sports School, in close partnership with the Singapore Table Tennis Association.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: This athlete-centric approach ensures he does not have to choose between academic success and sporting excellence.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Zhou Jingyi, a fellow paddler at Paris 2024, also highlights the critical support system that Home of Team Singapore aims to provide.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Jingyi has decided to take her GCE "O" level examinations with support from Singapore Sports School while she recovers from her injuries post-Olympics.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: It is crucial that Home of Team Singapore formalises and expands such support in close partnership with the respective NSAs.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: By integrating educational support with world-class training facilities and programmes for all athletes, we can ensure that young athletes like Izaac and Jingyi can continue to develop while balancing the demands of training, recovery and education at appropriate phases of their lives.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Similarly, Amita Berthier was able to return home to her alma mater at the Singapore Sports School in the final months leading up to the Paris Games, leveraging its boarding and training facilities as well as the tutelage of Oleg Matseichuk, the national team's foil head coach under Fencing Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: These kinds of partnerships allow our athletes to train at the highest level while having access to resources that enable them to grow mentally, physically and emotionally.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: In the spirit of celebrating sporting excellence in Singapore, it is important to recognise that many of our national athletes do not have full-time sporting careers.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: They are often modern supermen, superwomen, daytime students and workers and night-time athletes.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Still, they continue to achieve outstanding results, on par with many international teams, many of whom are full-time athletes.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: One example is our national Dragon Boat team, which consists entirely of part-time athletes and coaches.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: After work on weekdays, five days a week, they hold three-hour practices at the Kallang.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: On weekends, they even train more vigorously with double two-hour sessions per day.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Their hard work is evident from the impressive results in the international arena.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: As we look forward to the next major sporting platform, the Asian Games, we must continue to support the plethora of teams that represent our nation.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The waters at Kallang and our new Home of Team Singapore, together with the various national training centres around Singapore, will be crucial in supporting these teams in their sporting endeavours.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: It is inspiring the next generation of Singaporeans to embrace sports as a way of life, not just as spectators but as active participants, starting from our schools.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Much of our talent acquisition happens within the schools.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: In doing so, we can capture the imagination of our youths so that they are able to compete regularly in our own National Stadium and to hope that, one day, they will represent Singapore on the world stage.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Our Olympians will also continue to play an important role in building the next generation of athletes through school visits, mentorship programmes and public engagement.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: We hope that these collective efforts will push for the next bound of sporting excellence for Singapore and ensure that they become role models, inspiring children across the island to pick up a racket, a ball or a bow and arrow and to believe that they, too, can reach the top.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: The Home of Team Singapore will also be well-placed to provide the space for coaches, parents and support staff to be equipped with the tools they need to nurture athletes.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: New sports science and sports medicine facilities will also help on this.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: And the Home of Team Singapore is at the very heart of its future.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: To our athletes, thank you for reminding us that, in the face of adversity, there is always greatness within us.

speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
text: Your victories inspire us all to strive for better, to work harder and to unite as a nation in the pursuit of excellence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I would also like to extend a warm welcome to you at Parliament House, a place that serves as a home away from home for all of us fortunate to represent the people of Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As athletes, you have proudly represented our nation on the global stage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I hope you feel a strong sense of belonging here, knowing that your contributions, just like ours, are valued and celebrated in this place.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Your participation in the 2024 Summer Olympics brought immense pride and joy to our little nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: All of you have demonstrated remarkable physical, mental and emotional strength and determination throughout your journeys to Olympic and Paralympic success.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Your path has been marked by years of rigorous training.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Your resilience, commitment and ability to overcome challenges and excel under pressure are a testament to the power of human determination.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: As role models, you inspire others with your achievements and dedication.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The Games transcend borders, cultures and politics and inspire billions of people across the globe with their message of friendship, solidarity and fair play.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: In Singapore's diverse and multicultural society, these values of unity, mutual respect and peaceful competition resonate deeply.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The Olympics remind us that despite our differences, we can come together as citizens of the world and not citizens defined by abstract borders.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Our athletes, through their courage and commitment to take risks, push limits and strive for greatness, are an embodiment of Ali's wisdom.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore's participation in the Games is a testament to our ongoing commitment to fostering athletic talent, promoting a healthy lifestyle and showcasing our nation's progress.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Our athletes have become national heroes, inspiring new generations to embrace sports and strive for greatness.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Their success demonstrates the power of sports to transform lives, foster national pride and unite us in celebrating excellence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The Motion also recognises the family members, coaches and other support staff.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: They have spent many hours training, advising and supporting our athletes, often in the background and without recognition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Their belief and support are frequently the bedrock upon which our athletes have built their success.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: It is, therefore, only right that we shine a light on their contribution and acknowledge the indispensable role they play in our sporting ecosystem.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Some just want to keep fit, hang out with their friends or just give it a try because it is enjoyable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: While we absolutely need to have systems in place to identify and support potential or future Olympians, we do not want to inadvertently drive children and young people away from sport because of pressure to always be faster, stronger, better.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Sport, no matter the level, should always be fun, not a burden.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: You may be a weekend player or a beginner or someone trying to pick up a new sport.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Whatever your level, so long as you have interest in sports, there will be something for you here".

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The Singapore Safe Sport Commission continues to do commendable work in this area through policy, training and education, complaints handling and accreditation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: However, evidence-based safeguarding needs to be embedded across all sports and at all levels and this is lacking.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: We need to be able to do this and for this to be accepted as the norm by players and athletes, parents and coaches.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Doing so will not only reduce the risk of harm to children and young people playing sport, but importantly, will improve both their enjoyment of sport and their performance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: You have done us proud, but more importantly, you have done yourself proud.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: You are the elite in your field and I hope that you will remember Paris 2024 with delight and satisfaction, and more importantly, I hope you had fun.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: I also wish all our athletes the very best for whatever comes next on their remarkable journey.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: There is an old Chinese saying that goes “文无第一 , 武无第二”.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Loosely translated and interpreted, it means that there is no absolute number one in the arts and literary world, while being first is all that matters in the pugilistic or martial arts world.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Today, not many engage in martial arts fights and competitions anymore.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The second part of this phrase is often used to apply to the world of sports and to sportsmen and sportswomen.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It is nice to win, but there is more to sports than being first or winning medals.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Sports is also about forging our spirits in the crucible of competition and yes, defeat as well.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: When you go through hardships and decide not to surrender, that is strength”.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Let us give pause to what the “Governator” said here, which is almost counter-intuitive, “Strength does not come from winning”.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Everyone loves a winner and everyone loves to see the athletes achieve victory and the celebration that ensues.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Our celebration often centres around victories and talent.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But as Mr Schwarzeneggar said the athlete does not get stronger in victory.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: They do not even get stronger because they have talent.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: He said that one gets stronger when one struggles and go through hardships and not surrender.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: On one hand, we are here to celebrate our Olympians and Paralympians’ successes and victories in Paris, but on the other hand, we are also here to give praise to them for overcoming hardships and struggles and not surrendering, and in the process develop strength in body, soul and spirit.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This is especially true for our Paralympians, who despite facing challenges in life, choose to take the bull by its horns and face life with positive energy and become a Paralympian in the process.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: They have decided triumphantly that they will overcome all odds with verve and spirit.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Which is why I suppose the motto of the Paralympics is “spirit in motion”.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Her achievement at the Paralympics showcased the “spirit” of her journey of growing up with cerebral palsy, picking up boccia as a co-curricular activity, competing at the national, regional and eventually on the international stage, at the Paralympics.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Very importantly, her family who have been supporting her throughout this journey, played a vital role in her quest to overcome all odds and succeed.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The saying loosely translated into English is as follows: "When Heaven is about to confer a great responsibility on a person, it will first make the person endure hardship in spirit, exhaust his muscles and bones and experience hunger.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This is so that this person can cultivate a resilient spirit and enhance his capabilities." It is a more poetic and detailed way of expressing what the "Governator" has said.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It can also be used to describe what every successful athlete knows – the road to sporting success is paved with pain, deprivation, suffering and yes, even defeat.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: What is important is the will to get up and try again and again, to compete again and again, and eventually achieve success from the ashes of defeat.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It is the spirit of resilience and not giving in to defeatism, of not surrendering, but to rise from defeat, that is worthy of our celebration and honour.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: And it is also this spirit of resilience that Singapore has as well, that has made Singapore what it is today.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Sports is a microcosm of life and sports holds many lessons for us, for every generation of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This is why it is important that we inculcate the qualities that are to be found in great sportsmen and sportswomen into the fabric of our society; that of fair play, resilience, guts and teamwork.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Aside from learning from our defeats and rising up again, there are also lessons to be learnt from winning.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In this context, we can learn from Yip Pin Xiu.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I understand CMT disease leads to progressive muscle and sensory loss.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I think Pin Xiu has probably lost muscle mass and strength over the editions of Paralympics that she has won gold medals in.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Yet, she continues to defy the odds with the strength of her will and her discipline and dedication to training.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: As Singaporeans, we can all learn from Pin Xiu.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: As a country, Singapore has serious limitations of space and lack of natural resources.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: No matter what we do, these limitations remain with us.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But that does not mean our fates need to be determined by these limitations.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: With the same discipline and determination as Pin Xiu, Singapore can continue to come up tops in many ways in these uncertain times.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We can continue to meet challenges that come our way with positivity and overcome them by the strength of our collective will.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: At this juncture, I like to declare that I was a director of Yeo Hiap Seng Limited when the company started to sponsor Max in his sports activities.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: With the energy and fearlessness of youth, he is already charting new paths and peaks in his sporting career.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I am very confident that he will achieve more sporting glory for himself and Singapore in the years to come.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Like Max Maeder, Singapore is a young country.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Being a young country, we should not fear going into uncharted waters at high speeds, as long as we keep our heads level and our sight on what is important and what is the final goal.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Yes, there will be choppy waves along the way and sometimes we can even lose a bit of speed and direction, but as long as we have the wherewithal to stay the course and if necessary, to make adjustments along the way, we will get to where we need to be, where we want to be.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: He spoke about the differences and maybe the disparity in the incentive schemes.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I respect what he said and today is a happy occasion.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I do not hope to get into an intense and heated debate.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But let me respond by way of a tennis match.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In the early part of this year, I think in early February or late January, there was the Australian Open tennis final.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: During that game, Jannik Sinner was playing Daniel McDevitt.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: He was lost the first two sets, 3-6, 3-6.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In the third set, at one point, it looked like he was gone, finished.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: He was going to lose the third set and it was game over.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But then his coach shouted from the stands, "Weather the storm!

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: And therefore, became the first Italian to win the Australian Open.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Because I have learned from that tennis game that in sports, you always have two opponents.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: You have to overcome what is inside yourself.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: (In Mandarin):   The topic of sports is a significant one, a topic for the entire nation.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We must approach it carefully and thoughtfully, always prioritising the interests of the athletes and the people.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Within the sports family, there is no 'I' or 'you', only 'we', because we are a team.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The performance of our athletes this time has brought great joy, sunshine and new hopes to the people.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Therefore, I want to express my gratitude for our athletes' dedication, because you have brought new hope and insiprations.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: For your toil, your spirit, and your contributions, I extend my deepest gratitude to all of you.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I believe that your spirit is not just for the present, nor for 10 years, nor even for 100 years; it is eternal, and will last for generations to come. : Sir, in conclusion, I would like to share a song.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I was just driving the other day and this song came on the radio and I thought maybe I will use it today.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: For those of us old enough, I think you will know this song.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It is a song by Simon and Garfunkel.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It was very popular in the early 1970s.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It is a Spanish song titled, "El Condo Pasa".

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: For those of us old enough, you will know this song.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But the lyrics of the song are very interesting.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It goes something like, "I would rather be a sparrow than a snail.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I would rather be a hammer than a nail.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I would rather be a forest than a street" and I was thinking of today's Motion because, I am certain, hand on heart, for every athlete here, for every sports official here, for every family here, they can put hand on heart that they would rather be competing in the red and white colours of Team Singapore.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: For a moment, I thought you were going to sing, Mr Sitoh.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Yip Hong Wing, Ms Poh Li San, for your thoughtful sporting suggestions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Assoc Prof Razwana, for reminding us that sports should always be fun.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Jean See, Ms Hazel Pua, for your support.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, for your impassioned interventions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And of course, Ms Denise Phua, who not just was passionate in her speech, but she is so passionate that she came in Team Singapore colours as well today.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are all great suggestions which my team and I will take back and we will consider thoughtfully and take on board in the course of looking at the proposals and policies that we will have to advance sports.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I thought I would take up a response on two points which most of the Members have spoken about.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And the first is on our disability sports landscape.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Ms Denise Phua and Mr Keith Chua, in particular, noted that it is important to encourage children in our SPED schools to take up sports from a young age.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Ong Hua Han also suggested adopting a more structured approach to encouraging children with disabilities in mainstream schools to do sports.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In addition, I think Mr Ong Hua Han also mentioned that we have to raise awareness and understanding.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I can see why, because our children do not have, from a young age, a bias.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I think what is needed for them is to gain greater understanding and empathy, and also being able to be equipped with how to deal with a situation when they see a person with disability, how do you interact, how do you make the first move, how do you break the ice and how do you come together and socialise and form a community.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I think these are important steps that we will take and we believe that the platform of sports provides us a great way in which we can do this.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Keith Chua also noted that we can do more for persons with disabilities in the community.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It focuses on preparing SPED students for good health and life outcomes through lifelong sports participation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This early intervention can ensure that these children can access sports from a young age, cultivate a good habit and cultivate a culture for sustained and lifelong sports participation.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They include the Learn to Play programme, the annual Play Inclusive campaign that I spoke about, the Inclusive Sport Festival, which has itself also been integrated into the mainstream Get Active Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, it is no longer just about normal ability sports, but also special ability sports within our mainstream programmes like Get Active Singapore, which is a very popular programme.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And as I said earlier, as we look forward towards the launch of the DSMP, we will make further announcements on what else we are doing to enhance the disability sport landscape.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The second point I would like to respond to would be the incentive awards.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: First of all, as Ms Usha Chandradas pointed out, this is put up by non-government entities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They decide on the funding, the appropriate level, the structures and the terms on which this is done.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Between the Olympic and the Paralympic structure, there are differences.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But these differences do not mean one is necessarily better than the other.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the Olympics, for example, the first and only gold that is rewarded under the incentive programme is the first gold for $1 million.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, it is different, not necessarily comparable in the same way.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are also decided by the private sector on a range of different considerations.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: They have to think in terms of whether this is sustainable, is this an incentive programme that drives the right behaviour and how long term can this be?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Bearing in mind, for example, that if you compare the Paralympics with the Olympics, just in swimming alone, there are 141 Paralympic swimming events for which medals are awarded, as opposed to 37 in the Olympics.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, when the private sector, as well as Tote Board, looks at this, these are amongst the considerations that they have in mind.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim also spoke about equalising, and I think several other Members as well.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: With reference to some data, I think there was an article cited by Ms Usha Chandradas.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim spoke about the experience in Canada.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Let us not also forget that even as we look at trying to find parity, let us not forget where we start and where we are today in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Like Ms Chandradas says, Singapore is amongst the highest, if not the highest, in terms of the incentive scheme amounts in absolute terms.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Assoc Prof Lim spoke about Canada, but I think Assoc Prof Lim would know that Canada's incentive for a Paralympic gold is $20,000.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I am not sure whether Canada looks at the second or third golds as we do.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Other countries, like in Japan, mentioned by Ms Chandradas, their gold is at $20,000; Korea is at $50,000; France is at $100,000; and Australia is at $15,000.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, let us not also miss the wood for the trees.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have been pushing the amounts up over the years.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I can understand and appreciate entirely why Members have said let us find parity.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Because there is, in fact, no difference between the way in which our para athletes train, put effort, make sacrifices as well as our Olympic athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But let us not also lose sight of the amounts in absolute terms and how much we support our athletes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I also want to explain why we have taken the position that we have left the incentive schemes to the private sector and to the Tote Board to handle.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These awards, based on each major game, are set up and, as Members know, the games are cyclical.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At each game, like the Olympics, there might be a gold medallist or there might not be a gold medallist.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But the amounts that are committed will have to be put aside and have to be provided for, and you cannot use them, and because you cannot use them, you cannot deploy the funds elsewhere.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These are all spendings that are committed and that, every year, are spent to improve the infrastructure and landscape for both para and disability sports as well as able-bodied sports.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is an investment that the Government is committed to.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is not if you win an award, not whether; but it is a commitment that we make.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: If you put aside sums and think about whether or not I need to provide for "x" number of gold medals each cycle, these are sums that will not be able to be deployed.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And more importantly, we also take the approach that when you have an incentive programme, it is good, and we applaud the various supporters and corporates who come forward to help us in this effort.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But it is also rewarding people who are more or less at the end of the journey winning a gold medal.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, I hope that clarifies the position on the incentive schemes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These plans, we believe, will help us lift the entire base altogether.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will find a new baseline and in order to do this, we want to permanently shift the baseline so that we are no longer looking at vagaries or depending on each year, whether there are certain sports that may be in major games or otherwise, performances may then vary.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We want to permanently shift the baseline upwards.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: My colleagues and I at MCCY are convinced that the best years of sports lie ahead of us.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Ong Hua Han, in his speech earlier, spoke about how we have not even heard about kitefoiling until some months ago, before the Olympics.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Most of you know that I look after a constituency at Marine Parade.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: One day, when I was there a couple of months ago, after the Olympics, I saw a young boy.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: He tied a string to a plastic bag and he was running up and down the beach with the plastic bag.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I asked him what he was doing and he said, "I am kitefoiling."   So, it has that power to engender, to inspire and to break new ground.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I think that is the power of sports.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is something that the medium of sports is uniquely positioned to give us and we thank our athletes and all of the supporters, the many stakeholders in this room, in this Chamber today – family, friends, officials, coaches – everyone in that village or town that I spoke about.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We thank all of you very much for being here, for being part of this journey and we look forward to working with you even more, even further, as we take Singapore sports further forward.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: Earlier, the Minister mentioned that the percentage of Singaporeans engaged in sports at least once a week has improved significantly.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: I believe it was from over 50% to over 70%.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: For example, I have heard from many friends and relatives that it is practically impossible to book a badminton court under ActiveSG.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: To Ms Poa's point, yes, we are working towards refurbishing old ones to build more courts, build more facilities and also having newer ones.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I mentioned Toa Payoh, there is one in Punggol, Sengkang and various places.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But obviously, you can almost never cater enough because each time you look at a badminton court – four persons on the court.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I, as the Minister looking after sports, amongst the number one emails I get is precisely in the vein of what Ms Poa is asking for.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Can we have more facilities for badminton, for floorball, for tchoukball, and so on?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In a sense, I look at it as a good thing – that we have been quite successful in encouraging Singaporeans to be active in sport and want to take part in sports.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will do our best to catch up in terms of facilities, but we are defined by a finite set of resources on this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I appreciate that the amounts we offer are indeed comparatively higher relative to the other nations that Minister Tong mentioned.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: First, it is also true that we are both richer and win less medals overall, unfortunately, than these nations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: And so, in absolute terms, this should make the burden just somewhat more affordable.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: To be clear, I am not innocent of the very real budgetary constraints that we face in raising and implications of raising the amounts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
text: I will only ask Minister Tong if he would at least agree with the principle of equalising awards.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, these are steps that we are taking to bridge the gap if there is one, but I would not necessarily say that our focus is only on making sure that the incentives are equalised because there is a danger in that which is the point I was making to you earlier, Prof Lim, that in trying to strive towards equality, you have missed the woods for the trees – which is where we are already today.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Would you rather have equality or would you rather want substantive support that is being given to para athletes?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I will have a word and see whether that is possible, but I also want to make the point.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: It is not just a single source of success every time a medal is won.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As the Speaker, I cannot join the debate, but I just want to say to our Olympians and Paralympians, your family and support team, I salute you, this House salutes you and Singapore salutes you.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think we deserve a longer break now.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I propose to take a break now and I will suspend the Sitting and will take Chair at 3.50 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended at 3.22 pm until 3.50 pm.
